title: Instruction synthesis scribbles
content:
Quick context and goals:
- Personal scratchpad for trying compact instruction templates + tiny few-shot banks for common consumer-facing tasks (summarization, tone conversion, instruction-following).
- Want to understand brittle modes when we apply quantized model variants + high batching under latency SLO.
- Keep examples reproducible for eval harness (see Confluence link above).

Design notes / principles I want to test:
1) Make instructions orthogonal to examples — separate signal channels: one explicit instruction block + an examples block separated by a clear delimiter.
2) Prefer short, high-salience examples (3–5 shots) and test with 0/1/3/5 to measure diminishing returns.
3) Probe tokenization-edge prompts (emoji, code markers) to see if chunking breaks KV cache reuse.
4) Compare directive-first vs. persona-first phrasing for alignment with user intent.

Experiment matrix (to run later):
- Models: redwood-lite-3b-quant, redwood-medium-7b, redwood-alpha-13b
- Temperatures: 0.0, 0.2, 0.6
- Few-shot set sizes: 0, 1, 3, 5
- Prompt framing: instruction-only / instruction + examples / persona + instruction + examples
- Metrics: exact-match on instruction output (for structured tasks), ROUGE-L for summarization, manual severity labels for hallucination cases

Notes-to-self: token budgets matter for embeds vs gen routes — prefer compressed examples (short bullets) when targeting <200 token prompt windows.

Example templates (early drafts):
--- Template A: directive + example separator ---
INSTRUCTION: Rewrite the input text to be friendly and concise. Do not add facts.
EXAMPLES:
Input: "The Q3 numbers were a bit lower than forecast but still positive overall given headwinds."
Output: "Q3 missed forecasts slightly but remained positive despite headwinds."

Input: "We will pivot to new channels to drive engagement next month and hope for lift."
Output: "We'll shift to new channels next month to boost engagement."

----
Prompt assembly: [INSTRUCTION]

-- user_input --

Notes: separate examples clearly with 'Input:' and 'Output:' labels to help models learn mapping. Works well in alpha-13b, brittle in 3b-quant (tends to hallucinate additions).

--- Template B: persona + examples (try for creative revoice) ---
You are a customer-friendly support writer. Rewrite the message to sound warmer and shorter. Keep facts exactly as given.
EXAMPLES:
Input: "I couldn't sign in to my account despite trying multiple times."
Output: "Sorry about the sign-in trouble — we'll help you get back in quickly."

Follow with user message.

Failure case catalog (observed):
- Overzealous compression: model removes qualifiers (e.g., "potential risk" -> "risk"). Severity: medium. Trigger: instruct 'be concise' without 'preserve hedging'. Fix: append "Preserve hedging words (may, could, potential) unless explicitly asked to remove."
- Hallucinated actions: adds steps not in input (e.g., "reset password" suggested though not mentioned). Severity: high for support content. Trigger: persona framing + high temp. Fix: explicitly forbid adding actions: "Do not invent steps or facts."
- Repetition loops in 3b-quant: outputs repeat phrases when prompt includes emoji or special tokens. Severity: low/annoying but increases token cost. Workaround: sanitize non-ASCII or wrap in triple-backtick code fence when examples contain emoji.

Small few-shot bank for 'rewrite for clarity' (3-shot compact):
1) In: "We noticed the service degraded during the window." Out: "We saw service degradation during the window."
2) In: "The team will investigate and revert with updates." Out: "The team will investigate and follow up with updates."
3) In: "Please find the attached docs for more info." Out: "See the attached documents for more information."

Hypotheses to test (ranked):
- H1: Explicit 'do not add facts' line reduces hallucination rate by >30% at temp 0.2 for alpha-13b.
- H2: 1-shot chosen from the same domain yields most marginal gain vs. a generic example set of 3.
- H3: Quantized 3b models will benefit more from rigid labeling (Input:/Output:) than freeform examples.

Ad-hoc experiments I ran (notes):
- Ran 50 prompts on redwood-lite-3b-quant (temp 0.2) using Template A + 3-shot bank above. Observed 22% hallucination (mostly small added actions).
- Same prompts on alpha-13b at temp 0.0: hallucination 4%, but more conservative phrasing (sometimes verbose).

To-dos / follow-ups:
- Turn H1 into a small A/B in the eval harness (Ben to add a flag in prompt generator).
- Add a 'preserve hedging' sentinel into Template A and rerun mini-batch.
- Try the persona-first variant with alpha-13b at temp 0.0 and evaluate ROUGE-L vs baseline.
- Capture a few representative failure examples as unit tests for regression alerts (link in linked_artifacts).

Random scratch ideas:
- Try bilingual examples: same few-shot examples in English + Spanish to see if multilingual weighting helps when user input is code-switched.
- Explore 'microshots': 1-line examples that teach the model to prefer conservative rewrites (e.g., explicitly include the word 'may' in outputs when it exists in input).

Notes to self: keep this doc personal — later I'll formalize good patterns into a 'prompt-style-guide' for eng docs. Save current short examples into the eval harness under 'rewrites/compact-3shot'.

End of scribbles.
